chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb, from Ibn Riʾāb, from Al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasār, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, that he said:

Regarding a slave who wounds a free man, he said: “If the free man wishes, he may exact retribution from him; and if he wishes, he may take him, if the wound encompasses his value. But if it does not encompass his value, his master shall ransom him.”

He said: “If his master refuses to ransom him, then the wounded free man shall have his due from the slave in proportion to the indemnity of his wound, and the remainder belongs to the master. The slave is sold, the wounded man takes his right, and the remainder is returned to the master.”

key_terms.افْتَدَاهُ: his master compensates for him by paying ransom or indemnity
key_terms.بِرَقَبَتِهِ: with respect to his full value or person
key_terms.حُرًّا: a free person who was injured
key_terms.دِيَةِ: financial indemnity due for the injury
key_terms.عَبْدٍ: a slave whose legal liability is discussed in the ruling
key_terms.مَوْلَاهُ: his master, who bears financial responsibility in the case

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a slave injures a free man in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out the legal ruling for a case in which a slave wounds a free person. It explains the options of qiṣāṣ or financial compensation, and clarifies how the slave’s value and the master’s responsibility are treated when the injury does or does not amount to the slave’s full value.
